title: Energy + Token Efficiency Scorecard: A10 / L4 / A100 / H100
content:
Summary:
This is a working scorecard focused on the energy-to-token tradeoffs for four primary instance families we commonly evaluate: A10, L4, A100, and H100. Goal: produce a compact reference for product and infra to inform instance-mix recommendations and pricing sensitivity modeling ($/token, tokens/sec, tokens/sec/W).

Scope:
- Synthetic throughput tests (gpt-like 1.3B/7B/13B weights) at 2k and 8k context lengths.
- Default precision: fp16 baseline. Additional rows for int8/4 quant where available.
- Steady-state KV cache hit assumptions: 0% (cold), 30% (mixed), 70% (warm).
- Unit econ: includes instance amortized hourly cost + fixed infra overhead (networking, storage) rounded to a per-token estimate for representative workloads.

Quick takeaways (working):
- L4 shows best tokens/sec per watt for conversational-ish flows (shorter context), largely due to power efficiency on burstable workloads.
- A10 is very cost-competitive for low-latency moderate-throughput use cases (small models, light concurrency).
- A100 and H100 remain the best absolute throughput choices; H100 gives the best throughput at highest power draw (sweet spot for large-batch inference).
- Quantization to int8/4 moves the needle strongly on $/token for A100/H100; smaller effect for L4 (already optimized).

Scorecard table (representative numbers, see raw bench links):

| Instance | tokens/sec (7B, 2kctx) | tokens/sec (7B, 8kctx) | $/token (7B, 2kctx) | perf/W (tok/sec/W) | notes |
|---------|------------------------:|------------------------:|-------------------:|-------------------:|-------|
| A10     | 1,150                 | 820                   | $0.000012         | 2.1               | cheapest-hourly, good for low concurrency
| L4      | 980                   | 700                   | $0.000009         | 3.5               | most efficient per-watt for short contexts
| A100    | 3,400                 | 2,700                 | $0.000018         | 1.6               | high throughput; quantization yields ~30% $/token savings
| H100    | 5,200                 | 4,100                 | $0.000023         | 2.3               | top throughput; best for large-batch and long-context

Notes on methodology and caveats:
- Token/sec measured with continuous-batching driver (latency SLO 150ms p95). Raw numbers are median across 5 runs.
- $/token is back-of-envelope: (instance_hourly_cost + infra_overhead_hourly) / (tokens_per_hour_observed) + small margin for egress. We used instance prices from 2024-09 public price sheet (internal rate card).
- Perf/W here is tokens/sec divided by average measured board-level power draw during the run (Watts). Power draw measured via IPMI hooks + rack PDUs where possible; where not available we used vendor TDP + 15% ops overhead.
- Warm-cache assumptions reduce effective token cost by ~18–40% depending on model and reuse patterns.

Recommendations (short):
- Interactive chat (p95 latency <200ms, <10 RPS per model shard): prioritize L4 + A10. L4 as primary (efficiency), A10 to absorb very low-latency requests.
- High throughput batching (bulk embeddings, offline reranking): provision A100/H100 pools. Use H100 when context or model size pushes utilization high ( >70% peak).
- Cost-targeted mixed fleet: start with 60% L4 for steady traffic + 40% A100 reserved for batch windows. Backfill with A10 for sudden spiky load.
- Enable int8/4 quant profiles on A100/H100 for batch-heavy infer where quality loss is acceptable — validate with evaluation harness.

Operational guidance / config knobs to include in the optimize recommender:
- Auto-quantization candidate flag per model (passes unit tests before recommending)
- Cache TTL and prefix caching defaults tuned by observed reuse rate (default 45s for chat workloads)
- Dynamic routing policy: latency-first for <50ms SLOs, cost-first for >500ms SLOs.
- Suggested autoscale thresholds: target 70% device utilization for A100/H100 pools, 55% for L4/A10 to preserve latency headroom.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Validate power measurements for L4 across multi-vendor machines (Dell vs GCP instances differ notably).
- Run the same workload with offload-kernel variants (NVidia MIG-like configs) to see per-slice perf/W.
- Add 13B model rows to understand non-linear scaling for larger weights.
- Get updated internal rate card (Q1 2025) to refresh $/token projections.

Next steps (near term):
1) Run warm-cache bench across entire atlas of models (1B/3B/7B/13B) and push CSV to /shared_drives/product/optimize/raw-benchmarks/energy-token-2024Q4.csv (owner: Marcus).
2) Add an "instance-mix simulator" tab to the optimize runbook Excel that consumes the CSV and outputs per-customer $/month delta for switching mixes.
3) Productize two recommendation templates: (a) latency-first fleet; (b) throughput-first fleet.

Notes to self: keep this doc lean — most of the artifacts will be the CSVs and the simulator. This file is a high-level scorecard for quick referencing in conversations with infra and pricing.

Raw experiment tags and pointers:
- bench-run: 2024-10-01-energy-token-v2 (driver: /infra/bench/driver_v2.py)
- sample config: batch=32, max_tokens_per_request=512, kv_cache=false
- perf trace: s3://redwood-bench/2024-10/energy-token/trace-20241001.zip

If you’re reviewing: check the perf/W math in the A100 rows (I suspected power over-estimation).

-- Lena
